newsitem.title: USA: FIGURE SKATING-ELDREDGE WINS U.S. FIGURE SKATING TITLE.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-ELDREDGE WINS U.S. FIGURE SKATING TITLE.

text.p: Todd Eldredge, receiving just five first-place scores from the nine judges after a shaky performance, still managed to win his fourth U.S. Figure Skating Championship on Saturday.
Michael Weiss, moved from fifth place after the short programme to win the silver medal on the strength of four first-place marks.
Weiss, who has competed on the senior level for three years, came close to landing the first quadruple toe loop in U.S. National competition, but did not cleanly finish the jump on one foot.
Dan Hollander, successfully defended his bronze medal in a performance that included seven triple jumps.
Weiss and Hollander will join Eldredge to represent the United States at the World Championships next month in Lusanne, Switzerland.
Eldredge's title caps a very successful season where he won the Ultimate Four competition, France's Trophy Lalique and the Continents Cup.
Yet, he had a weak performance in Saturday's finals. "Things didn't feel right today," he said.
He did not complete any triple-triple combination, turned his triple flip into a double, had to rescue the landing of an off-axis triple salchow and a wobbly landing on this triple lutz.
The judges still rewarded him with a range of 5.9s and 5.8s for technical merit. Eldredge was one of many top competitors to have trouble with landings.
Eldredge has 10 days to prepare for the Champion Series Final -- the culmination of five international competitions since last October. The winner of the Series receives $50,000.
Eldredge is expected to face stiff competition at the Series finals from Russian Ilya Kulik and former World Champion Elvis Stojko from Canada.

Weiss will not participate in the final, but at the World Championships he may force Olympic gold medalist Alexi Urmanov, Stojko and Kulik to include the four rotation jump in their long programmes. Eldredge has been practicing the quad but does not feel the jump is necessary to win the gold medal.
"The quad has become more important since Kurt Browning landed the first one in 1988," said Eldredge's coach Richard Callaghan. "It is not necessary, but it is a big help."
